text:
maria: FYI overnight aurora nightly job flagged a tail regression on small-batch CI, p95 up ~12% vs baseline. CI link: https://ci.internal/runs/aurora-3912345678 :eyes:
ci-bot: [alert] aurora/nightly-smallbatch — p95 latency +12% (detected 03:12 UTC). Suspect kernel scheduler or batching change.

maria: tagging @devon @logan — can someone pick this up for a quick triage?

devon: I'll take first pass. grabbing logs now. anyone know if the KV cache experiment was on for that run?

maria: cache TTL was default. no active cache-experiment for that pipeline.

logan: ping — I left a couple of micro-optimizations in #PR-478 last week that touched the batcher. could be related.

sree: repro suggestion: run the nightly bench with --sample-rate=0.2 and --trace=flame, here's the command I use:
```
./tools/run_bench --suite=smallbatch --seq-len=512 --iterations=200 --sample-rate=0.2 --trace=flame
```
run on a core node.

devon: running that now on a replica (n2-highgpu). posting flame when done.

infra-bot: Node pool aurora-core had a rolling update around 01:50 UTC; 2 nodes replaced. No errors reported.

logan: my PR touched batch scheduling and a fallback path for low-latency mode. I can roll it back if we see correlation.

maria: let's avoid immediate revert unless flamegraph implicates that code path. devon, if you can point to stack some samples, we can decide.

devon: sample capture done. flame link: https://perf.internal/flames/3912345678. initial look: heavy time in kernel-sched wakeup and our batcher spin-wait.

logan: hmm, spin-wait — maybe the fallback path didn't pick up because the kv-cache returned partial hit. adding a quick probe to log batcher fallback decisions.

maria: can you push a debug-only build to nightly next run? small change — just extra logging. no behavioral changes.

logan: will do. patching now and will queue a redeploy. ETA ~25m.

sree: also request that we run an isolated benchmark with quantized variant (q8) to see if quantization affects scheduling patterns — different kernel sizes change scheduling.

devon: good call. I'll kick that after the debug-run.

maria: thanks everyone. outcome options after debug run: 1) revert PR-478, 2) adjust fallback thresholds, 3) schedule infra follow-up if node update correlates. please add recommended action to the run comment. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: [run queued] aurora/nightly-smallbatch (debug build) — triggered by @logan. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/aurora-3912345699

devon: logging shows spikes align with node replacement windows from infra-bot earlier. adding infra tag. @infra-bot any chance the new kernel version bumped timer granularity?

infra-bot: kernel version on replaced nodes: 5.15.0-88 -> 5.15.0-92. No known timer changes in release notes, but I can roll one node back if needed for repro.

maria: don't rollback yet. let's see debug-run + q8 run. if both reproduce, priority high and we'll plan revert.

logan: debug build queued. will post results here.

maria: thanks — will hold an async triage doc and assign follow-ups after runs. if anyone wants to take ownership of the revert patch, say so.

sree: happy to own a revert if flame implicates PR-478.

devon: got a short-term mitigation idea: increase fallback timeout from 3ms -> 6ms to reduce spin. I can prototype in a patch for fast rollback.

maria: add that as option 2 in the triage doc. I'll create the doc and link it here after we see debug output.

logan: debug run completed — flame shows >40% samples in batcher spin path during the p95 windows. pushing a minimal logging patch now.

ci-bot: [run finished] aurora/nightly-smallbatch (debug) — p95 still +11%.

maria: OK that suggests infra + scheduling interplay, not purely logic bug. let's run the q8 isolated test next.

devon: q8 run started. will report back.

sree: added a short checklist in thread: 1) reproduce w/ debug flags, 2) rerun on rolled-back kernel node, 3) prepare revert PR, 4) propose fallback timeout patch.

maria: perfect. I'll update with links and owners in ~1h once q8 finishes. thanks all for quick reaction. :heart:
